orders.perOrderHelp: Order totals, customer and status. Good for accounting summaries.

orders.importSubtitle: Bring orders over from another system
orders.historicalHelp: Records the orders and their lines without changing inventory. Use this for past orders whose goods have already left, so current stock stays as it is. Webhooks and plugins are not notified.
orders.notifyIntegrations: Notify webhooks and plugins about each order
orders.notifyIntegrationsHelp: Sends an order.created webhook and runs plugin order hooks for every imported order, as if it were entered by hand. Turn off if the orders already exist in the connected systems.
orders.linesNoteRow: Each row is one order line, with the order number, external reference, date, status and customer.
orders.linesNoteTotals: Order totals (subtotal, tax, shipping, total) are repeated on every line of the order. When summing totals, count each order once, for example only rows where Line is 1.
orders.linesNoteVariant: Variant SKU and Variant Title are filled only for lines sold as a variant.
orders.requiredSku: and a product_sku or variant_sku on every row.
orders.ruleGrouping: One row per order line. Rows with the same external_reference form one order. Order-level columns (date, status, customer, order_tax, order_shipping, notes) may be repeated or given on one row only.
orders.ruleAllOrNothing: The whole file is checked first. An order with any invalid row is not imported at all, and each problem is reported by row.
orders.ruleDuplicates: An external_reference that was already imported is skipped, so importing the same file twice never duplicates orders.
orders.ruleCustomers: Customers are matched by email. Otherwise a new customer is created.
orders.ruleStock: Stock is deducted like a hand-entered order, and an order without enough stock is not imported. Historical imports and cancelled orders never change stock.
orders.ruleIntegrations: Historical imports never send order.created webhooks. Other imports send them by default; untick the option to skip them.

users.ruleRole: role is the base role: member, manager or admin. Blank means member.
users.ruleRoles: roles lists custom role names, separated by ; or ,
users.rulePasswords: Never put passwords in the file. New users get a random password and choose their own through the emailed link.
users.ruleDuplicates: Emails that already have an account, or appear twice in the file, are skipped with a warning.
users.ruleEscalation: You can only assign roles you are allowed to assign: non-admins can import members only, with roles no wider than their own permissions.
